identity: A single hadith from Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Iman): a three-link isnad (Abd Allah b. Muhammad -> Abu Amir al-Aqadi -> Sulayman b. Bilal -> Abd Allah b. Dinar -> Abu Salih -> Abu Hurayra -> the Prophet) followed by a two-clause aphoristic matn. 44 tokens, no <NL>, single paragraph. Doctrine genre L (hadith/isnad), the graded precedent being doc_27a114d4e376.
law: Isnad-and-matn law. (1) Each transmission verb opens a unit: every clause-initial qala hadathana / hadathani starts a new sentence, so the boundary falls on the personal name that closes the preceding link, immediately before qala. Precedent L1 gold: hadathana Ismail || qala haddathani Malik b. Anas an ammihi Abi Suhayl. (2) an-links never cut: an X is a bare PP carrying no predication whatsoever, so it fails the conjunct-weight test and rides inside the unit opened by its transmission verb; the L1 gold keeps an ammihi Abi Suhayl inside its unit. (3) Formulaic honorifics (radiya llahu anhu, salla llahu alayhi wa-sallam) are never boundaries. (4) The short-tail brake 0b is SUSPENDED in this genre: the L1 gold cut off a two-token unit. (5) The matn-introducing qala is a speech verb and opens its own unit with its quoted content attached (E3). (6) Inside the matn, wa cuts normally (L2) whenever the conjunct carries its own predication (master law, section 0 conjunct-weight test).
reasoning: Four decisions. (a) @4 and @9: three qala hadathana openings means three units. This is the exact shape of the L1 gold, same collection and same formula, and E1/B2 reinforce it -- a repeated opening word is a repeated boundary. That the first unit is only five tokens and the second only five is irrelevant, since the L1 gold itself cut off a two-token unit, which is direct graded evidence that the short-tail rule does not exist in isnad. (b) Inside 10-34 I take no cuts. Each an X is a bare prepositional phrase with no verb, no khabar, no adverbial frame of its own -- the pure bare-conjunct case that the conjunct-weight test sends to NO CUT, exactly like wa-l-Iraq wa-Australia as bare nouns. The L1 gold confirms by keeping an ammihi Abi Suhayl inside the unit. I also refuse the tempting cut after the dangling an at index 29: H1 dangling-function-word cuts require parallel list items to follow, and a single an al-Nabi is not a list. (c) @34: two independent rules converge. Under L1 this qala is the chain-closing transmission verb, and under E3 a speech verb opens a unit while its quoted content stays glued to it -- so the boundary goes before qala, not after it, and al-iman bid un wa-sittuna shu ba stays attached. (d) @39 is the only genuinely contested site, so I argue it fully. The tail wa-l-haya u shu batun mina l-iman is four tokens, squarely inside the numeric range of the 0b short-tail brake, and this is a famous short saying often quoted whole, both of which pull toward merging. I reject the merge. The brake 0b is written with two explicit scope conditions and this fragment satisfies neither: it is stated to hold in running prose only, and it requires the stranded fragment to be non-parallel and dependent-feeling. This fragment is a complete nominal sentence -- mubtada al-haya u, which is a brand-new topic distinct from the previous subject, khabar shu batun, and its own PP frame mina l-iman -- and it stands in deliberate chiastic parallel with the clause before it, iman...shu ba against haya u shu ba...iman. On conjunct weight it is as far from bare-noun wa as it is possible to get; it is the ministry-of-Vietnam case (its own subject plus its own frame, a unit even with no verb), not the wa-l-Iraq case. Two genre-matched golds settle it: L2 states that narrative wa inside the matn cuts normally and its gold gave a unit to the six-token wa-la yafqahu ma yaqulu hatta dana, and B2 gave separate units to the short parallel nominal clauses wa-l-basaru... / wa-l-shammu yudriku l-rawa iha / wa-l-dhawqu yudriku l-tu uma, with the explicit ruling that parallelism defeats the short-tail rule. Checklist item 4 also binds: my calibration is 7:1 wrong in the merge direction, the default is CUT, and I must actively justify not cutting -- here I cannot. I also checked the D2/B8 earlier-candidate correction and found no competing boundary one to five tokens before @39, so there is no earlier cut to prefer instead. (e) @43 is the final token and is mandatory.
